evidence.excerpt: Alignment accuracy at structural variant breakpoints affects downstream SV calling quality, yet most aligner benchmarks focus on SNPs and small indels. We constructed a synthetic benchmark dataset of 2 200 breakpoint-spanning read pairs spanning 110 curated SV loci (deletions, tandem duplications, and inversions ranging from 50 bp to 50 kb) derived from a validated clinical variant database. Four short-read aligners were evaluated: two BWT-based and two graph-based tools. We measured mapping quality distribution, soft-clip rate within 200 bp of breakpoints, and downstream SV call concordance using two SV callers. Graph-based aligners achieved 12–18 percentage point higher recall at inversion breakpoints compared to BWT-based aligners, but produced 2.3× more multimapping reads genome-wide, increasing false-positive SV calls by 9 %. Runtime and memory differences between aligner classes were substantial: graph-based alignment required 3.1× more peak RAM and 2.4× more wall time per sample. Results are tabulated per SV class and size bin.
